skills.name: jstack-advice
skills.description: Strategic and design counsel—stakeholder-aware options, tradeoffs, and a clear recommendation. Use for leadership/EM/product/design dilemmas, prioritization of principles, 1:1 or exec prep, or when the user wants named perspectives (not generic brainstorming). Grounds in team KB and gbrain when configured; never invents org policy.

skills.name: jstack-announcement-review
skills.description: Review an announcement for tone, accuracy, and channel fit. Flag legal/PR risks if external.

skills.name: jstack-announcements
skills.description: Draft channel-ready or email-ready announcements from rough notes, respecting tone policies and internal/external distinction.

skills.name: jstack-ceo-brainstorm
skills.description: "Alias jstack:ceo-brainstorm — CEO persona + executive tone, then superpowers:brainstorming. Use when the user wants exec-lens ideation."

skills.name: jstack-computer-use
skills.description: Route computer-use requests — native macOS/desktop UI (CUA) vs web automation (jstack workflows, Playwright MCP) vs a saved JSON workflow definition under config/workflows/.

skills.name: jstack-computer-use-cua
skills.description: "Operate CUA (computer-use): Cua Driver (macOS AX + MCP), CuaBot (Docker + Xpra), Cua sandboxes (Python SDK / cloud CLI). Verbs: setup, test, execute, status, restart, destroy. Use when the user mentions cua, trycua, cua-driver, cuabot, computer-use, sandbox, macOS desktop QA, Electron, native app automation, MCP desktop control, TCC, or debug/QA repro outside the browser. Parent router: jstack-computer-use."

skills.name: jstack-counsel-review
skills.description: Multi-persona review (CEO/PM/eng/QA/design) with synthesis and tensions. Not vote-counting by title.

skills.name: jstack-crew
skills.description: Inspect and manage the background Slack agents (crew) that watch a DM and answer in it — list, show, create, edit, enable, disable, remove agents, check status, explain why a message got no reply, and halt everything. Use when the user asks about "my agents", "background agents", "Ralph", "crew", "why didn't it respond", or wants to add/disable an agent. Do NOT use to compose or send a Slack message, and do NOT use to switch the crew to live posting — that is a deliberate human step (`jstackc crew go-live`).

skills.name: jstack-crew-onboarding
skills.description: Conversational wizard for standing up a NEW crew (background Slack) agent — names it, shapes its persona through a few characterizing questions instead of a blank system-prompt, sets its workspace, confirms the owner-only default, then drafts the exact `jstackc crew agents add …` invocation and persona file for the user to review. Never runs it. Use for "add another crew agent", "set up a new background agent", "I want a second Ralph". Do NOT use to edit an existing agent, view status, enable/go-live, or diagnose why one didn't respond — that's all `jstack:crew`. Do NOT use for the general first-run jstack setup wizard — that's `jstack:onboarding`.

skills.name: jstack-custom
skills.description: Execute a custom routine from its config/schedules/<id>.json definition plus the routines block in config/defaults.json. If schedule JSON is invalid, return a fix, not a fake result.

skills.name: jstack-design
skills.description: Route a design request to the right sub-skill (figma-handoff, visual-single-page-html). Not for writing component code.

skills.name: jstack-end-session
skills.description: "End the current session: summarize, flush carryover items, optionally run eval hooks."

skills.name: jstack-engineer-report
skills.description: "Generate an individual engineer report: shipped, WIP, blockers, next. No invented metrics."

skills.name: jstack-engineering
skills.description: Quick composite snapshot of CI status, PR queue, flaky tests, and revert risk from configured repos. For DORA-banded deep analysis with thresholds and trend context, use jstack:engineering-health instead.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-blast-radius
skills.description: Find what a change could break somewhere else — beyond the diff itself — before it ships: other callers of a changed function, other consumers of a changed schema/type, another language reading the same wire format, a feature flag three hops downstream. Then prove the one fact that makes it safe (or not) by running real code — grepping for callers, executing the function, running the affected test — never by writing a plausible-sounding paragraph. Use for "blast radius of X," "what could this break," or reviewing a small diff you don't fully trust yet. Do NOT use for in-diff correctness review (is this specific change right) — that is `jstack:review-code-review`. Do NOT use for verifying an arbitrary claim unrelated to a shipping change (a perf number, "did this fix it") — that is `jstack:engineering-verify-this`. Inspired by Cursor's `pstack` plugin's `blast-radius` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-compatibility-check
skills.description: Runs jstack.core's own sixteen structural/config gates (schema and config drift, write-gate and SRI security checks, agent/skill config-matrix and depth, chain and router integrity, description-reference, referenced-file, name-collision, prompt-wiring, and alias-drift checks) and blends the results into one weighted compatibility score plus a ranked "fix these first" list. Read-only — it only runs checks and reports; it never edits a file and never runs the slower legs of `bun run check` (typecheck, tests, format, evals, the a2a suite). For DORA-banded engineering health, use jstack:engineering-health instead; for bus-factor / knowledge-silo risk, use jstack:engineering-silo-scan instead; for the full CI chain including tests and typecheck, tell the user to run `bun run check` directly.
skills.whenToUse: "Also trigger on: 'is the skill catalog healthy', 'run the compatibility gates', 'score the repo's config/skill checks', 'what's broken across the gates', 'give me a fix-first list for the structural checks', or a request to summarize `bun run check` failures into one number."

skills.name: jstack-engineering-create-verification-skill
skills.description: Generate a project-local, checked-in skill that drives a project's real app, CLI, service, or TUI the way an actual user would — clicks, CLI invocations, API calls, or keystrokes — and defines what counts as proof for that mechanism (exit code + stdout, a screenshot/ARIA snapshot, a HAR file, a captured network log) so future work has a scripted, evidence-backed way to confirm behavior instead of "looks right" or a stub that always reports success. Use when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior, or the user says "make a control skill for this repo," "give this project a verification skill," "generate a verify-skill for X," or "/create-verification-skill". Do NOT use to settle one specific claim right now — that is `jstack:engineering-verify-this` (a single ad hoc VERIFIED/NOT VERIFIED/INCONCLUSIVE call, run once and discarded); this skill instead produces a reusable, checked-in skill that can verify many future claims about the same project. Do NOT use to author the SKILL.md mechanics yourself (frontmatter fields, file placement, chain contract shape) — delegate that structure to `jstack:skill-creator`; this skill's own job is the interview and the proof-standard content that goes inside the generated file. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `create-verification-skill` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-fix-ci
skills.description: Diagnose why a specific, already-open PR's or branch's CI check is red: pull the actual failing log (not just the summary line) via `gh pr checks`, `gh run view --log-failed`, or a third-party check's own external details URL, root-cause it, and apply exactly one focused fix. This is the single-iteration diagnose-and-fix unit that `jstack:engineering-loop-on-ci` calls repeatedly until every check is green — use this skill directly for one failing check, one pass; use `jstack:engineering-loop-on-ci` when the ask is to drive every currently-failing check to green automatically, across however many rounds that takes. Do NOT use for a pre-merge correctness review of a diff whose CI hasn't run yet or is currently green — that is `jstack:review-code-review` (or `jstack:thermonuclear-review` for a high-stakes pass), which hunts for defects in a diff rather than diagnosing why an already-red check is red. Do NOT use to make a check pass by adding `continue-on-error`, disabling the check, or `--no-verify` — none of those are an acceptable outcome here, even when the underlying issue turns out to be flaky or environmental rather than a real defect. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `fix-ci` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-fix-merge-conflicts
skills.description: Resolve merge/rebase/cherry-pick conflicts non-interactively where the correct resolution is genuinely unambiguous — reading every conflicting hunk with real git commands (`git status`, `git diff`, `git log --merge`, conflict-marker greps) before choosing a side — regenerate lockfiles with the package manager rather than hand-editing them, then validate by actually running the target repo's build/typecheck/test command before calling it done. Use when a branch has unresolved conflicts and needs a reliable path to a buildable state. Do NOT use to guess through a real semantic conflict — when both sides made substantively different logical changes to the same code, stop and ask rather than picking a side. Do NOT use for the deep line-level correctness/security read of the merged result — that is `jstack:review-code-review` (single deep read) or `jstack:thermonuclear-review` (high-stakes, six-lens); this skill's job stops at a clean, buildable, non-conflicted state. Do NOT use to force-push or discard uncommitted/unpushed work as a shortcut — check what's actually there before touching anything, and never run a destructive git operation without explicit human confirmation. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `fix-merge-conflicts` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-health
skills.description: DORA-banded engineering health — the four keys (deploy frequency, lead time, change-failure rate, MTTR) reported as independent bands with the metric, measurement window, and threshold behind each, paired with leading indicators (PR review latency, CI flake trend). For a quick composite snapshot without DORA bands or trend context, use jstack:engineering instead.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-loop-on-ci
skills.description: Watch a branch or pull request's CI checks and iterate — inspect each failure, delegate the actual diagnose-and-patch work to `jstack:engineering-fix-ci`, re-check, and repeat until every check is green or a stopping condition is hit. Use when the user says "loop on CI," "keep fixing this until it's green," "watch this PR and fix failures," or pastes a PR/branch and asks you to babysit it through to a passing build. Do NOT use for a single diagnose-and-patch pass on one already-known failure — that unit of work is `jstack:engineering-fix-ci`, which this skill calls repeatedly; if the user only wants that one pass, invoke it directly instead. Do NOT use for a read-only health snapshot across all configured repos (CI status, PR queue, flaky tests, revert risk) — that is `jstack:engineering`, which never actively loops on or fixes one specific PR. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `loop-on-ci` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-show-me-your-work
skills.description: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work — a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result) — so a human who wasn't watching can reconstruct what happened and trust the result without rerunning the work or reading the whole transcript. Local scratch by default; commit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for autonomous or multi-phase runs, "show me your work," or any task a human will review after stepping away. Do NOT use this for anonymous aggregate metrics (token counts, latency, success rate) — that's `telemetry/`, a different mechanism with a different audience. Do NOT use this for personal reflection — that's `jstack:self-diary`. This is a task-scoped audit trail for a reviewer who needs to trust a specific run, not a metrics pipeline or a personal journal. Inspired by pstack's `show-me-your-work` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-silo-scan
skills.description: Bus-factor / knowledge-concentration scan — per-module bus factor and silo ratio from trailing commit and review-authorship spread, weighted by change frequency and fan-in. Read-only unless user approves comments. Not for detecting overlapping work on the same files or similar tickets/PRs.

skills.name: jstack-engineering-verify-this
skills.description: Prove or disprove a specific claim about running system behavior with fresh, repeatable local evidence: restate the claim falsifiably (condition, metric, threshold), capture a baseline artifact from the old state and a treatment artifact from the new state with the same command and environment, compare the raw artifacts, and return exactly one verdict — VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED, or INCONCLUSIVE. Use when the user asks "verify this," "prove it works," "did this fix it," "show me the evidence," or a bug-fix/perf/behavior claim needs a real before/after, not a read of the diff. Do NOT use for a vague, unmeasurable claim ("the code is cleaner") — ask for a falsifiable claim first. Do NOT use for skill/agent regression testing — that is `evals/a2a/` (this repo's own fixed-case harness), not a one-off runtime claim. Do NOT use for jstack's own fixed structural gates (schema drift, chain integrity, name collisions) — that is `jstack:engineering-compatibility-check`. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `verify-this` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-eval-report
skills.description: Generate a 9-grid evaluation report with growth framing. Sensitive — mark manager-only if needed.

skills.name: jstack-executive-research-brief
skills.description: "Alias jstack:executive-research-brief — CEO lens + executive tone, then jstack competitive research for leadership."

skills.name: jstack-federated-search
skills.description: Multi-provider federated search — selects N backends (Jira, Notion, Slack, GitHub, Glean, Google, DuckDuckGo, gbrain, knowledge_base, etc.) from the user query or explicit flags; delegates one constrained subagent (or isolated tool sweep) per provider; merges hits, ranks relevance to the question, structures a single answer. Supports --raw to skip synthesis. Reads jstack.config.json mcp_servers and integrations; does not invent credentials. Not for knowledge-base-only lookups — use jstack:knowledge-search for that.

skills.name: jstack-figma-handoff
skills.description: Turn a Figma design into an implementable handoff — named components and variants, token references, state coverage, and the accessibility contract each state must meet. Load before design-to-code or MCP Figma work; chain to figma-use when the host provides it. Not for writing the component code or editing the Figma file itself.

skills.name: jstack-figure-it-out
skills.description: Design and run a rigorous, scoped, one-off plan for a big or unusual task that doesn't match any existing skill, playbook, or SOP in the catalog. Frames the actual goal/constraints/done-state in 1-2 sentences, picks the smallest set of steps a reviewer could verify, runs them in order checking each before the next, and hands back a plain-prose audit trail naming what was verified vs. assumed. Not for a task a real skill already covers — check the catalog first and chain to that skill instead. Not for authoring a new **permanent** skill file — use `jstack:skill-creator` instead. Not for a chain that will recur — use `jstack:workflow-builder` instead once the same one-off has run more than a couple of times.
skills.whenToUse: "Also trigger on: 'no skill fits this', 'this is a one-off', 'figure this out', 'make a plan for this weird task', 'nothing in the catalog covers this', an ask that spans multiple unrelated systems with no existing chain, or a request explicitly declined by a more specific skill's out-of-scope note."

skills.name: jstack-granola-daily-summary
skills.description: End-of-day rollup across multiple meetings' notes or Granola exports into one digest. For a single Granola export from one meeting, use jstack:meetings-granola instead.

skills.name: jstack-healthcheck
skills.description: "Run jstack doctor + integration smoke test. Classify: P1 broken, P2 degraded. Output one Slack summary line."

skills.name: jstack-hygiene-claude-code-hygiene
skills.description: Audit a user's actual Claude Code setup — skills, agents, hooks, slash commands, and settings.json permissions — for what is broken, stale, unused, or duplicated, then walk through a numbered fix plan before touching anything. Use for "audit my claude setup," "clean up unused skills," "is my claude code config stale," "find duplicate skills," "why do I have two agents that do the same thing," "do any of my skills have zero eval coverage," or a periodic hygiene sweep before a skill-authoring push. Two phases, always in this order — Phase 1 is a read-only audit that runs freely and never edits or deletes anything; Phase 2 (actually deleting, editing, or regenerating a skill/agent/hook/permission) only happens after the user has seen Phase 1's findings and confirms each fix item individually. Not for authoring a brand-new skill from scratch (jstack:skill-creator) or opening the PR itself (jstack:plugin) — this skill diagnoses and plans, those two execute. Also trigger for "sweep my skills directory," "find dead agents," "check for orphaned reference files," "why is my settings.json so long," "check for broken chain contracts," "has Claude Code shipped anything new I'm not using," or any request to review/clean up/tidy the Claude Code setup itself (as opposed to reviewing a codebase or a PR).

skills.name: jstack-improve-claude-md
skills.description: Audit a project's CLAUDE.md against commits, session transcripts, and working-tree state, then propose ranked edits as a unified diff. Read-only by default; --apply is opt-in. Use when CLAUDE.md feels stale, when you have been correcting Claude on the same thing, or as a monthly hygiene routine.

skills.name: jstack-incident
skills.description: Route incident requests to the right sub-skill (retro, find-sme, oncall-summary).

skills.name: jstack-incident-find-sme

Use when asked "who knows this system" or "who should look at this incident." Do NOT use to page or message anyone, or to rank people by commit volume alone.

skills.name: jstack-incident-oncall-summary
skills.description: Summarize an on-call window from the configured Slack channel, incident tool, and schedule, grouping alerts and optionally investigating individual issues. Use for on-call handoff or end-of-shift summaries. Do NOT use to acknowledge or resolve alerts or change alert thresholds.

skills.name: jstack-incident-retro
skills.description: "Facilitate a blameless retrospective: timeline, impact, what went well, improvements, actions with owners and dates."

skills.name: jstack-ingest-all

skills.name: jstack-init-session

skills.name: jstack-intake
skills.description: Convert unstructured feature/ticket requests into shaped ticket fields. Split bundled requests into separate candidates. Also when shaping a feature idea, PRD snippet, messy notes, or Slack thread into ticket-ready fields (before Jira create).

skills.name: jstack-jira
skills.description: Route Jira requests to the right sub-skill (get, create, update, intake, transition, notify, append). Ask one question if ambiguous. Also when the user mentions tickets, issues, JQL, triage, filing bugs, sprint backlog, status transitions, or commenting on an issue.

skills.name: jstack-jira-append
skills.description: Append a structured content block (meeting notes, checklist, update block) to an existing Jira issue's description or as a formatted comment. For a plain one-line comment, use jira/update instead.

skills.name: jstack-jira-create
skills.description: Create a Jira issue from user input or intake payload, with dup-check and template pre-fill from config.

skills.name: jstack-jira-get
skills.description: Fetch Jira issues by key or JQL filter and return a structured table of status, assignee, priority, and links. Look up, fetch, or filter Jira issues by key or JQL — read-only, no status changes.

skills.name: jstack-jira-intake
skills.description: Convert raw text or a jstack:intake payload into Jira-ready fields (summary, description, AC, labels).

skills.name: jstack-jira-notify
skills.description: Draft a Slack or email notification about a Jira event (status change, assignment, comment) for user approval.

skills.name: jstack-jira-transition

skills.name: jstack-jira-update

skills.name: jstack-knowledge
skills.description: Route knowledge requests to the right sub-skill (intake, process, search, self-knowledge, team-knowledge, ingest-all, skill-finder, reflect). Also for wiki/runbook search, doc Q&A from repo URLs, gbrain or Notion knowledge, note ingestion, deduping entries, or team knowledge graph.

skills.name: jstack-knowledge-intake
skills.description: Ingest raw text into a structured record (title, body, tags). Flag PII/secrets before storage. User says "save this," "capture this," "log this decision," "note this down," or pastes raw text/a decision and wants it turned into a structured, storable record — not when they're asking a question that should be answered from existing knowledge (that's knowledge/search).

skills.name: jstack-knowledge-process
skills.description: Deduplicate, merge near-duplicates, and set canonical links across gbrain/Notion entries.

skills.name: jstack-knowledge-reflect
skills.description: Mine THIS session's own transcript for durable, reusable lessons once a task has landed — not mid-task. Runs 2–3 independent adversarial reviewer passes over every candidate lesson (did it actually work, was the approach sound, was there a cheaper way), then one synthesis pass that buckets each candidate into Accepted / Rejected / Backlog, and stops for explicit human confirmation before handing the Accepted list to `jstack:team-knowledge` or `jstack:self-knowledge` for the actual write — this skill never writes to gbrain itself. Use after a hard debug, a long multi-step task, or a project wrap-up to ask "what should a future session already know so it doesn't repeat this mistake or redo this work." Trigger phrases: "reflect on this," "what did we learn," "do a retro before we close this out," "mine this session for lessons," "capture what we just learned." Not for knowledge pasted in from outside this session — use `jstack:knowledge-intake`; not for the write itself — use `jstack:knowledge-process`, `jstack:team-knowledge`, or `jstack:self-knowledge`; not for reading back logged history across many past sessions — use `jstack:skill-creator-retro`.

skills.name: jstack-knowledge-search
skills.description: Look up answers from configured knowledge sources (local paths, doc URLs, GitHub repos) using jstack.config.json knowledge_base — cite sources; do not guess from general knowledge when a source list exists. For storing notes use knowledge-intake, not this skill.

skills.name: jstack-manager-report

skills.name: jstack-meetings
skills.description: Route meeting requests to the right sub-skill (prepare, transcribe, granola-highlights, action-items, post-slack, notion-highlights, store-note, one-on-one-transcript, transcripts-ingest).

skills.name: jstack-meetings-action-items

skills.name: jstack-meetings-granola

skills.name: jstack-meetings-notion-highlights
skills.description: Insert meeting highlights into a Notion DB with title, date, participants, and transcript link.

skills.name: jstack-meetings-one-on-one-transcript

skills.name: jstack-meetings-post-slack
skills.description: Draft a meeting summary for a Slack channel with tone from prompts/tones/. Do not post without user approval.

skills.name: jstack-meetings-prepare

skills.name: jstack-meetings-store-note

skills.name: jstack-meetings-store-personal

skills.name: jstack-meetings-store-team
skills.description: Save meeting notes to team gbrain or Notion per config. Follow team storage rules.

skills.name: jstack-meetings-transcribe

skills.name: jstack-metrics

skills.name: jstack-morning-kickoff

skills.name: jstack-my-metrics

skills.name: jstack-notion

skills.name: jstack-notion-article

skills.name: jstack-notion-one-on-one

skills.name: jstack-notion-performance

skills.name: jstack-notion-planning

skills.name: jstack-notion-project

skills.name: jstack-notion-report

skills.name: jstack-notion-setup
skills.description: "Build a Notion team HQ + private vault tree from the typed template catalog. Surface-aware: team-side artifacts must land inside a Notion teamspace (via anchor page), private vault stays workspace-private. Wires all ids back into jstack.config.json."

skills.name: jstack-notion-sprint
skills.description: Create or update a sprint page in Notion with goal, scope, and Jira sprint id when provided.

skills.name: jstack-notion-standup
skills.description: Create or update a standup page or database row in Notion using the configured standup template and optional gallery template page. Use only when asked to write a standup into Notion. Do NOT use to post the standup to Slack (`jstack:meetings-post-slack`).

skills.name: jstack-notion-team-note
skills.description: Create a lightweight team note in Notion. Suggest ADR for binding decisions instead.

skills.name: jstack-notion-team-report

skills.name: jstack-onboarding

Use for "get me set up", "onboard me", "I just installed jstack", or when jstack.config.json is missing. Not for editing an existing working config (use jstack:update-config) and not for diagnosing a specific doctor failure (use jstack:setup).

skills.name: jstack-pe
skills.description: Route a people/performance-engineering request to the right sub-skill — report-context to assemble/validate a reporting window and team scope against pe.* config, or pe-recon for a proactive team-scoped digest sweep. Not for writing performance narrative about a named individual.

skills.name: jstack-pe-pe-recon
skills.description: Proactive multi-source recon sweep — Notion, Slack, and whatever else is configured, routed exactly the way jstack:recon routes them — scoped to the Platform Engineer team/group set in pe.teams, synthesized into a skimmable local HTML digest (exec summary first, then categorized findings with links) that opens in the browser for async review. Use for "PE weekly digest," "what's going on for my team," "platform engineering recon," or a scheduled PE catch-up. Do NOT use for a one-off narrow question ("what's the status of PROJ-123", "any P1s in #eng-alerts right now") — that's a single lookup, not a team-scoped digest; call `jstack:recon` directly instead.

skills.name: jstack-pe-report-context
skills.description: Validate and normalize PE / team report JSON against schemas/pe; gate skills until pe.configured is true. Building or validating performance/team report context JSON before render or Notion/ HTML publish.

skills.name: jstack-plugin
skills.description: Open a PR to jstack.core or jstack.gusto using distribution.github from config; block secrets via path_deny_globs. Contributor has local changes and wants a PR against the configured core or gusto distribution repo.

skills.name: jstack-pr-review-canvas
skills.description: Generate an interactive HTML walkthrough of a GitHub PR — categorized file cards (core vs mechanical), reviewer annotations, rendered diffs with moved-code detection, and a review checklist — served locally so a reviewer can click through it instead of reading a raw diff. Use when the user pastes a GitHub PR URL/number and asks for a review, walkthrough, or visual summary, or says "review this PR," "make this easy to review," or "walk me through this diff." Do NOT use for the deep-read line-level defect hunt itself — `jstack:review-code-review` (or `jstack:thermonuclear-review` for a high-stakes pass) does the actual finding; this skill is the presentation layer on top of that reading, not a substitute for it. Do NOT use to publish or share the generated HTML anywhere outside this machine — it can contain proprietary diffs and stays local. Inspired by Cursor's `cursor-team-kit` plugin's `pr-review-canvas` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-prioritize
skills.description: Rank a list using RICE, WSJF, value/effort, or a user-provided rubric. Show scores and cutline.

skills.name: jstack-project
skills.description: "Cross-surface project status (Notion/Jira): RAG health, 3 risks, 3 asks, milestone table."

skills.name: jstack-project-report
skills.description: "Generate a stakeholder 1-pager: RAG status, milestones, risk register snapshot."

skills.name: jstack-project-review
skills.description: Review a project update for schedule, scope, risk, and stakeholder issues. Factual errors vs strategy issues.

skills.name: jstack-recon
skills.description: Read-oriented sweep across configured Slack, Jira, and similar integrations to answer "what needs attention"—P1s, stale work, open questions, and standup-ready action items. Produces a bounded summary plus an explicit action_items count line for evals. Does not open tickets, post to Slack, or change external state unless a different skill is invoked after user approval.

skills.name: jstack-report-design
skills.description: Choose a report's shape before its content — audience, sections, and which figures earn a place — before jstack:reports assembles the finished report. Use when the report's structure isn't decided yet, not for filling an already-decided shape with data.

skills.name: jstack-reports
skills.description: Route report requests to the right sub-skill (team-report, engineer-report, manager-report, project-report, eval-report, report-design, share-html-publish).

skills.name: jstack-research
skills.description: Route research requests to the right sub-skill (technical, competitive, user, spike, explain-codebase).

skills.name: jstack-research-competitive
skills.description: Competitive analysis with comparison table. Treat public info as potentially stale; never claim private competitor metrics.

skills.name: jstack-research-explaincodebase
skills.description: "Map a codebase top-down: entry file, packages, main flows, then one deep dive the user requested."

skills.name: jstack-research-spike
skills.description: "Time-boxed technical spike: hypothesis, method, go/no-go criteria up front. Report findings even if spike fails."

skills.name: jstack-research-technical
skills.description: "Structured technical investigation: architecture options, tradeoff matrix, recommendation with migration/operability risks."

skills.name: jstack-research-user
skills.description: Synthesize user interview themes with verbatim quotes (permission-aware). Distinguish frequent vs loud users.

skills.name: jstack-review
skills.description: Route review requests to the right sub-skill (code-review, project-review, announcement-review, counsel-review, codex-bridge, codex-review, thermonuclear-review, interrogate, pr-review-canvas, maintainability-audit).

skills.name: jstack-review-code-review
skills.description: PR workflow — seek (find review queue), appraise (file-by-file review with draft comments), polish (pre-push self-review vs default branch). Not to be confused with `jstack-review-codex-review` (one letter away), which gets a second opinion from the external codex CLI instead of Claude's own review.

skills.name: jstack-review-codex-bridge
skills.description: Low-level utility for invoking the external `codex` CLI (OpenAI Codex) as a second, independent AI collaborator and carrying a real multi-turn exchange with it via `codex exec` and `codex exec resume`/`codex exec fork`. Use only when a task specifically needs a second, independent model's opinion or output — not as a general shell-out mechanism for arbitrary tools, and not when Claude's own analysis already answers the question. Other skills (for example `jstack:review-codex-review`) build on this one instead of invoking `codex` directly.

skills.name: jstack-review-codex-review
skills.description: Get a genuinely independent second opinion on a diff or PR from the external `codex` CLI, built on `jstack:review-codex-bridge` — send the diff with explicit grounding/citation standards, work through any pushback with codex for a bounded number of rounds, and surface real, unresolved disagreement to the user instead of collapsing it into a fake consensus. Use when a change is genuinely worth a second, independent model's scrutiny and codex is installed. Do NOT use on trivial one-line/rename-only changes — say so and decline rather than manufacturing findings. Complements, not replaces, `jstack-review-code-review` (one letter away — Claude's own internal review persona); this skill's whole value is being a separate, external check.

skills.name: jstack-review-interrogate
skills.description: Run one rigorous correctness/quality review prompt through Claude (this agent) and the external `codex` CLI independently, once each, against the same diff/PR/file, then reconcile the two reads into an attributed triage table — agree-block (both models independently flagged it, higher confidence), disagree (both positions stated, not resolved by picking a side), single-model-flag (worth a second look, not dropped and not silently promoted), and praise. Mirrors `agents/review-counsel.md`'s reconciliation discipline (the agent `jstack:counsel-review` invokes for multi-persona synthesis — Prime Directives 4, 8, and 10) applied across MODELS instead of personas. Use when a diff/PR/file is worth a second, independently-reasoning model's read and a single one-shot comparison is enough. Do NOT use for a negotiated back-and-forth with codex across multiple rounds (fix / push-back / escalate, applying edits, resuming a thread) — that is `jstack:review-codex-review`'s job; this skill runs each side exactly once and never edits anything. Do NOT use for multi-persona (CEO/PM/eng/QA/ design) synthesis — that is `jstack:counsel-review`. Do NOT use on a trivial one-line/rename-only change — say so and decline rather than manufacturing findings.

skills.name: jstack-review-maintainability-audit
skills.description: Single-lens, deep structural-maintainability audit of a diff: hunts for a "code-judo" restructuring that deletes complexity rather than rearranging it, treats a file crossing the 1,000-line threshold as a presumptive blocker needing a stated reason, flags spaghetti-growth (ad-hoc conditionals bolted onto an unrelated flow) as a design problem rather than a style nit, is skeptical of thin/pass-through wrapper abstractions and cast-heavy type boundaries, and pushes on type/boundary cleanliness (unnecessary `any`/`unknown`/casts) when it affects maintainability. Use for "how maintainable is this," "is there a simpler way to structure this," "audit this for code-judo opportunities," or "is this file getting too big." `jstack:thermonuclear-review` can invoke this skill as its code-quality lens for extra structural depth beyond that lens's general complexity/debt pass; it can also run standalone on a diff/PR with no six-lens process at all. Do NOT use as a substitute for `jstack:thermonuclear-review`'s six-lens dispatch (security, compliance, performance, code quality, QA, AI-slop) when the ask is broader than structure — this is one deep structural lens, not a seventh lens in that roster, and does not touch security/compliance/performance/QA at all. Do NOT use for a routine PR with no structural-complexity question — `jstack:review-code-review` is lighter and sufficient there. Inspired by the Thermos plugin's `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review` skill, adapted to jstack conventions.

skills.name: jstack-routines
skills.description: Route to the right routine sub-skill (standup, weekly-digest, sprint-close, health-check, custom, morning-kickoff).

skills.name: jstack-scaffold
skills.description: Scaffold a new skill or plugin using org conventions and checklists. User wants to create a new skill pack or plugin structure.

skills.name: jstack-sdlc
skills.description: Map SDLC stages to evidence (tests, sign-offs, flags, migrations). Produce gate checklists, not Jira state changes.

skills.name: jstack-self
skills.description: Route personal productivity requests to the right sub-skill (diary, lookback, focus, eval, remember, tasks, explain, brag, impact-prep, draft-messages, tldr, recall).

skills.name: jstack-self-brag
skills.description: Daily or weekly activity brag from Slack, GitHub, and Jira mapped to config-defined impact dimensions; parallel gather; tiered PR labels; personal gbrain by default.

skills.name: jstack-self-diary
skills.description: Write a single journal entry to personal gbrain. Never auto-post to team channels.

skills.name: jstack-self-draft-messages
skills.description: Draft multiple tone/intent variants of a message the user wants to send to one specific person or small group — a Slack DM, an email, difficult feedback, an apology, a decline, an escalation — for a chosen venue and audience, each with an honest note on how the recipient might receive it. Use for "help me write this message," "draft a Slack DM," "how should I phrase this," "I need to tell someone X," or "help me push back on this without it landing badly." Do NOT use for formal org-wide announcements, product launches, or policy communications — those go through `jstack:announcements`, which applies tone policy and legal/compliance review this skill does not have. Never sends or posts anything; drafts only.

skills.name: jstack-self-eval
skills.description: Self-assessment on a 9-grid with one growth goal for next 2 weeks. Not formal HR input unless user says so.

skills.name: jstack-self-explain
skills.description: Short narrative of recent work for PR descriptions or standup, tying commits to user impact.

skills.name: jstack-self-focus
skills.description: Synthesize 2-3 focus blocks from tasks + gbrain, one explicit non-goal, and a timebox suggestion.

skills.name: jstack-self-impact-prep
skills.description: IC impact prep — Growth Check-in (quick) or Quarterly sweep with artifact gather, gap questions, config rubrics; personal gbrain default.

skills.name: jstack-self-knowledge
skills.description: Link personal GitHub activity and gbrain entries. No scraping private repos without token scope.

skills.name: jstack-self-lookback
skills.description: Review last N days of personal gbrain + calendar and surface patterns. Gentle, not therapeutic.

skills.name: jstack-self-recall
skills.description: Reconstruct a tight "where did I leave off" brief after a gap — a multi-day break, a context compaction, a fresh session — by combining live repo state (git log/status, open PRs), the local jstack memory store, and whatever recent conversation history the host makes available. Use for "catch me up," "what have I been working on," "where did I leave off," or before resuming work after a break. Do NOT use for a reflective review of the last N days' patterns and growth — that is `jstack:self-lookback`. Do NOT use to bootstrap a brand-new session's config (gbrain target, timezone) — that is `jstack:init-session`; recall reconstructs what already happened, it does not set up what happens next. Inspired by pstack's `recall` skill, adapted to jstack conventions and to host-agnostic sourcing (no assumption about where or how the host stores chat transcripts).

skills.name: jstack-self-remember
skills.description: Store a durable personal fact or decision in the local jstack memory store (jstack memory log), optionally also gbrain when configured. Refuses to write anything that looks like a pasted secret.

skills.name: jstack-self-tasks
skills.description: Roll up personal tasks from Jira + gbrain TODOs. Deduplicate and return top 5 with a parking lot.

skills.name: jstack-self-tldr
skills.description: Compress a prior Claude response or a long pasted passage in this conversation into a short, ranked bullet summary that ends with an explicit next-step offer, then keep every follow-up in the exchange concise instead of ballooning back into a wall of text. Use for "tl;dr", "summarize that", "give me the short version", "too long, summarize", or any ask to shorten output already produced here. Do not use on content that's already short (a sentence or two) — say so instead of manufacturing a summary of nothing — and do not use when the user asks for the FULL detail after already receiving a summary from this skill; that is a deeper-dive request this skill answers directly, not a new tl;dr to run.

skills.name: jstack-session
skills.description: Route to session init or end. Also when starting or ending a jstack session, choosing personal vs team gbrain target, or wrapping up with a session summary.

skills.name: jstack-setup
skills.description: "Repair an existing jstack setup: interpret a jstack doctor failure, fix a missing or corrupted jstack.config.json on a project that was previously working, or re-run MCP server discovery/health checks. No secrets in chat. Not for a brand-new user's first-time walkthrough (use jstack:onboarding) or editing an already-working config (use jstack:update-config)."

skills.name: jstack-share-html-publish
skills.description: Publish or download HTML via a share-some-html style MCP (update/get) or JSON-RPC curl fallback; writes all artifacts under a config-defined directory (default /tmp). Optional access password when the server supports it.

skills.name: jstack-shortcuts
skills.description: Route a named composite shortcut to its sub-skill (ceo-brainstorm, executive-research-brief). Each composite pins a specific persona plus tone. Not for generic brainstorming or research — use the underlying skill directly when no named composite fits.

skills.name: jstack-skill-creator
skills.description: Create or revise jstack plugin skills (SKILL.md) using repo conventions, Anthropic-aligned directives, and config-first rules. Use when adding capabilities, forking a skill, or fixing discovery/failure coverage — not for running product workflows.

skills.name: jstack-skill-creator-retro
skills.description: Read back the local jstack memory store (jstack memory search) plus recent eval reports and declined-edit history, and produce a self-improvement retro -- what's been learned, what recurred often enough to promote into a real fix, and what's still just a log entry. Use when the user asks "what have we learned," "do a retro on our skills," "what keeps coming up," or as a periodic hygiene routine. Not for a personal-life retrospective -- that's self/lookback.

skills.name: jstack-skill-finder
skills.description: Map vague user goals to specific jstack skills; prefer CLI skills index and domain routers. User asks how to do something or which jstack skill to use; keep answers to 1–3 skills with rationale. Do NOT use to perform the recommended skill's work.

skills.name: jstack-sop
skills.description: Route SOP requests to expectations or resources sub-skill.

skills.name: jstack-sop-expectations
skills.description: "Maintain role expectations docs: what success looks like, autonomy boundaries, escalation paths."

skills.name: jstack-sop-resources
skills.description: "Maintain resources docs: on-call, tools, how to get unblocked, SLA references."

skills.name: jstack-sprint
skills.description: Route sprint requests to the right sub-skill (prep, refinement, planning) -- capacity/goal planning, mid-sprint re-plan, or backlog refinement from Jira.

skills.name: jstack-sprint-planning
skills.description: "Sprint planning: capacity, commit vs goal, spill from last sprint with root causes."

skills.name: jstack-sprint-prep
skills.description: Pre-refinement prep — curate needs-refinement queue vs sprint goals, flag stale work, suggest new tickets for gaps, priority order draft.

skills.name: jstack-sprint-refinement
skills.description: Refinement ceremony — five questions per ticket, capacity snapshot, sprint-ready checklist; no bulk Jira writes without confirmation.

skills.name: jstack-sprintclose
skills.description: "Sprint close routine: velocity, spill, carry, retro hook. Do not fabricate demo links."

skills.name: jstack-standup
skills.description: "Generate standup content: yesterday/today/blocked from Jira+Slack. 3 bullets max per person. Draft only."

skills.name: jstack-team
skills.description: "Team snapshot: roster, on-call, sprint goal, dependencies. No individual performance color."

skills.name: jstack-team-knowledge
skills.description: "Build the team knowledge graph: link issues, ADRs, runbooks. Suggest hubs and flag stale pages."

skills.name: jstack-team-metrics
skills.description: Team DORA-style signals with caveats for sample size. Separate unplanned work % when labels exist.

skills.name: jstack-team-report
skills.description: "Generate a weekly team report: velocity, risks, dependencies, and 3 asks to leadership. Weekly update to leadership; sprint report; team status update; velocity and risk rollup for a manager or skip-level; 'what should I send my manager this week'."

skills.name: jstack-thermonuclear-review
skills.description: Dispatches a diff/PR/file set to six independent lenses in parallel — security, compliance, performance, code quality, QA/testability, and AI-slop detection — then combines them into one severity-ranked list, never a blended verdict. Every finding is attributed to the lens that raised it and cites concrete evidence. Use for a high-stakes change, a security-sensitive surface, or a pre-launch review — not a routine PR. For a routine PR, use `jstack:review-code-review` (single lens, lighter weight). For a cross-role ship/no-ship call without this skill's security/compliance/AI-slop depth, use `jstack:counsel-review`. This skill complements both; it replaces neither. Trigger phrases: "thermonuclear review," "exhaustive review," "audit this before we ship," "give me every lens on this," "security and compliance and everything review," "tear this diff apart," "pre-launch review," "review this like the launch depends on it."

skills.name: jstack-transcripts-ingest
skills.description: Ingest new transcript files from Google Drive (or paste) into meetings pipeline; classify source and route to child skills. New meeting transcripts arrived in Drive or user pastes a file; route to highlights, transcribe, or action-items flows.

skills.name: jstack-update-config
skills.description: Edit jstack.config.json with validation against config/schema.json. Show diff and rollback one-liner. Not for first-time setup — use jstack:onboarding. Not for a brand-new project with no config yet — that is jstack:onboarding's job.

skills.name: jstack-visual-single-page-html
skills.description: Build one standalone HTML file with React, Tailwind 4-style tokens, Chart.js/D3 via CDN, shadcn-compatible CSS themes, citations to design theory, report IA hierarchy, and typographic markdown rendering—not a Next.js bundle. User wants a single downloadable HTML dashboard, branded report viewer, slide-like page, or interactive viz page without a build step; mentions React Tailwind Chart.js D3 shadcn themes SPA CDN; asks for markdown on page with professional layout or report/presentation design.

skills.name: jstack-weeklydigest
skills.description: "Run the scheduled weekly digest wrapper around jstack:team-report: two-audience split, exec summary + links, unattended-safe."

skills.name: jstack-workflow-builder
skills.description: "Design or update multi-step team workflows (chains, routines, policies, approvals) from sprint, comms, SDLC, and incident patterns. Produces chain markdown and config-ready snippets — use after install to customize the plugin without editing skills by hand. Not for one-off Jira tickets. Not for browser/Playwright flows — that is `jstack-workflows-builder` (note the plural), which authors a clickable UI script; this skill authors skill-chain, routine, and policy definitions."

skills.name: jstack-workflow-execute
skills.description: "Run a saved workflow via CLI: preview, then execute with --yes through a spawned agent driving a browser-automation tool (e.g. Playwright MCP). After a workflow exists in config/workflows; user wants to run it from the agent or confirm CLI behavior."

skills.name: jstack-workflow-recorder
skills.description: Record user browser actions into a workflow definition, scrubbing captured secrets before saving and adding stability notes for generated selectors before promoting to CI. Use when the user wants to capture a flow by demonstrating it. Do NOT use to run the recording (`jstack:workflow-execute`) or hand-author steps (`jstack:workflows-builder`).

skills.name: jstack-workflow-viewer
skills.description: "Summarize what a workflow run log contains: steps taken and artifacts produced. Use to inspect a finished run by run-id. Do NOT use to re-run or edit a workflow, and never reconstruct a result for a run with no report."

skills.name: jstack-workflows
skills.description: Route workflow requests to builder, recorder, execute, or viewer. Also for Playwright-style flows, browser automation JSON definitions under `config/workflows/`, recording steps, or running jstack workflow.

skills.name: jstack-workflows-builder
skills.description: "Build a BROWSER workflow definition as JSON at `config/workflows/<id>.json`: start URL and ordered steps drawn from the six kinds the schema allows (goto, click, fill, wait, screenshot, ai). No credentials in the file. Not for skill-chain, routine, or policy design — that is `jstack-workflow-builder` (singular), a different skill one letter away."

skills.name: jstack-writing-humanizer
skills.description: Rewrites AI-sounding text into natural human professional prose by stripping a concrete, categorized list of banned patterns, including em-dashes used as comma/period substitutes, triadic "X, Y, and Z" rhythm, "It's not just X, it's Y" and "Whether you're X or Y" constructions, hedge/filler words ("leverage", "delve into", "seamless", "cutting-edge", "at the end of the day"), empty transitions ("Let's dive in"), and hollow closers ("Let me know if you have any questions!"), while preserving the source's exact meaning and facts. Use when asked to "make this sound less like AI," "remove AI writing patterns," "humanize this text," "this sounds robotic," or to edit the tone/style of an email, doc, Slack message, comment, or post. Do NOT use on source code, code comments, or config files; never touch those. Do NOT use on legal, medical, compliance, or other precision-critical text where an exact technical or legal term matters more than sounding conversational; flag that instead of rewriting it (see Out of scope).
